books.name: Genesis
books.when: Written for Israel in the wilderness, around 1400s BC; covers creation to about 1800 BC
books.big: God creates a good world, people break it with sin, and God starts his rescue plan through one family: Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and Joseph.
books.jesus: God promises a descendant of Eve who will crush the serpent (3:15) and a blessing for all nations through Abraham's offspring. Jesus is that offspring.

books.name: Exodus
books.when: Egypt and the Sinai desert, around 1400s BC
books.big: God hears his people's cry, breaks Egypt's grip, brings them out, gives them his law and comes to live among them in the tabernacle.
books.jesus: The Passover lamb whose blood saves points to Jesus, "our Passover lamb" (1 Cor 5:7). The tabernacle shows God dwelling with people, which Jesus fulfills (John 1:14).

books.name: Leviticus
books.big: A holy God makes a way for sinful people to live near him through sacrifices, priests and a set-apart way of life.
books.jesus: Every sacrifice and the Day of Atonement point to Jesus, the final high priest and the once-for-all sacrifice (Hebrews 9-10).

books.name: Numbers
books.when: The 40 years in the wilderness between Sinai and Canaan
books.big: Israel complains and rebels, and a whole generation dies in the desert, but God stays faithful and brings their children to the edge of the promised land.
books.jesus: Jesus compares himself to the bronze snake lifted up so people could look and live (John 3:14-15).

books.name: Deuteronomy
books.when: On the plains of Moab, just before Israel enters Canaan
books.big: Moses' farewell sermons: remember what God did, love him with everything, obey his word, and choose life.
books.jesus: Jesus quotes Deuteronomy to defeat Satan in the wilderness, and he is the prophet like Moses that God promised (18:15).

books.name: Joshua
books.big: God keeps his promise and gives Israel the land as they trust him, fight, and divide it among the tribes.
books.jesus: Joshua's name is the Hebrew form of "Jesus" (the LORD saves); Jesus leads his people into the true rest (Hebrews 4).

books.name: Judges
books.when: Israel before the kings, about 1370-1050 BC
books.big: A downward spiral: Israel turns to idols, gets oppressed, cries out, God sends a judge to rescue, and they fall again. "Everyone did what was right in his own eyes."
books.jesus: Every flawed judge shows the need for a perfect rescuer and king.

books.name: Ruth
books.when: During the time of the judges
books.big: A loyal Moabite widow and a kind Israelite redeemer show God's quiet faithfulness, leading to King David.
books.jesus: Boaz the kinsman-redeemer pictures Jesus, and Ruth is in Jesus' family line (Matthew 1:5).

books.name: 1 Samuel
books.who: Unknown, using records from Samuel, Nathan and Gad
books.when: Israel's shift from judges to kings, about 1100-1010 BC
books.big: Israel asks for a king like the nations. Saul starts strong and fails; God chooses David, a man after his own heart.
books.jesus: David, the shepherd king from Bethlehem, points to Jesus, the Son of David.

books.name: 2 Samuel
books.big: David's victories, God's covenant promising an eternal throne, then David's sin with Bathsheba and the family fallout.
books.jesus: God promises David a son whose kingdom will last forever (7:12-16), fulfilled in Jesus.

books.name: 1 Kings
books.big: Solomon's wisdom and temple, then his heart drifts, the kingdom splits, and prophets like Elijah confront idolatrous kings.
books.jesus: Jesus is greater than Solomon (Matthew 12:42) and the true temple.

books.name: 2 Kings
books.when: Elisha to the fall of Jerusalem, about 850-586 BC
books.big: Both kingdoms keep sinning despite the prophets; Assyria takes Israel and Babylon takes Judah.
books.jesus: Elisha's miracles foreshadow Jesus', and the surviving king at the end keeps David's line alive.

books.name: 1 Chronicles
books.when: Written after the exile, retelling history from Adam to David
books.big: For returned exiles: you are still God's people. Genealogies, David's reign and preparation for worship.
books.jesus: The focus on David's line and the temple points to Jesus, the Son of David.

books.name: 2 Chronicles
books.when: Written after the exile; Solomon to the exile
books.big: Judah's story told through its kings and temple worship: seeking God brings blessing, forsaking him brings ruin.
books.jesus: The book ends with permission to rebuild, a hope fully met in Jesus.

books.name: Ezra
books.big: God moves a pagan king to send exiles home; they rebuild the temple, and Ezra calls them back to God's word.
books.jesus: God keeping his people and his promises after exile sets the stage for Jesus.

books.name: Nehemiah
books.big: Nehemiah rebuilds Jerusalem's walls in 52 days despite opposition, and the people recommit to God's law.
books.jesus: Nehemiah's leadership and prayer show the kind of godly leader fulfilled in Jesus.

books.name: Esther
books.big: God is never named, yet he is clearly at work: Esther risks her life and the Jews are saved from genocide.
books.jesus: Esther stands in the gap for her people at great risk, a shadow of Jesus' far greater rescue.

books.name: Job
books.when: Set in the time of the patriarchs; date of writing uncertain
books.big: Why do good people suffer? Job loses everything, wrestles with God honestly, and finds that God himself, not an explanation, is the answer.
books.jesus: Job longs for a mediator and a living Redeemer (19:25). Jesus is the innocent sufferer who stands between us and God.

books.name: Psalms
books.who: David and others (Asaph, the sons of Korah, Solomon, Moses)
books.when: Written over about 1,000 years, gathered after the exile
books.big: Israel's prayer and song book: praise, lament, thanks, confession and trust, for every season of life.
books.jesus: Jesus prayed the Psalms and fulfills them: the King of Psalm 2, the sufferer of Psalm 22, the Lord of Psalm 110.

books.name: Proverbs
books.big: Practical wisdom for daily life, built on one foundation: "The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom."
books.jesus: Jesus is the wisdom of God (1 Corinthians 1:30), the perfect wise man.

books.name: Ecclesiastes
books.big: Life "under the sun" without God is meaningless smoke. Enjoy God's gifts, fear him and keep his commands.
books.jesus: Jesus brings the meaning and resurrection hope that Ecclesiastes longs for.

books.name: Song of Songs
books.big: A love poem celebrating the joy and commitment of love between a husband and wife.
books.jesus: Christians have long seen in it a picture of Christ's love for his bride, the church (Ephesians 5).

books.name: Isaiah
books.when: Jerusalem, about 740-680 BC, as Assyria threatened
books.big: God is the Holy One who judges sin, yet promises comfort, a suffering Servant and a new creation.
books.jesus: Isaiah is quoted all over the New Testament: the virgin birth (7:14), the child called Mighty God (9:6), the Servant pierced for our transgressions (53).

books.name: Jeremiah
books.big: The "weeping prophet" warns Judah for decades, watches Jerusalem fall, and announces a new covenant written on hearts.
books.jesus: Jesus inaugurates the new covenant of Jeremiah 31 in his blood (Luke 22:20).

books.name: Lamentations
books.when: Just after Jerusalem's destruction in 586 BC
books.big: Five poems of grief over Jerusalem's fall, with hope in the middle: God's mercies are new every morning.
books.jesus: Jesus wept over Jerusalem and bore God's judgment so his people could be restored.

books.name: Ezekiel
books.big: God's glory leaves the corrupt temple, judgment falls, but God promises new hearts, dry bones raised and his glory returning.
books.jesus: Jesus is the Good Shepherd Ezekiel promised (34) and the one who brings new hearts by the Spirit.

books.name: Daniel
books.big: Faithfulness in a pagan culture, and visions showing God rules history and will give an everlasting kingdom to "one like a son of man."
books.jesus: Jesus called himself the Son of Man from Daniel 7 more than any other title.

books.name: Hosea
books.big: God tells Hosea to marry an unfaithful wife and keep loving her, a living picture of God's relentless love for unfaithful Israel.
books.jesus: Jesus is the faithful husband who pays to bring his unfaithful bride home.

books.name: Joel
books.big: A locust plague is a warning of the coming Day of the LORD; return to God, and he will pour out his Spirit on all people.
books.jesus: Peter quotes Joel at Pentecost (Acts 2) when Jesus pours out the Spirit.

books.name: Amos
books.when: Northern Israel, about 760 BC, a time of wealth
books.big: God cares about justice: worship means nothing while the poor are crushed. "Let justice roll down like waters."
books.jesus: Amos ends with God rebuilding David's fallen tent, which Acts 15 applies to Jesus gathering the nations.

books.name: Obadiah
books.when: After an attack on Jerusalem, likely 586 BC
books.big: Edom gloated over Judah's fall, and God will judge pride; the kingdom will be the LORD's.
books.jesus: Jesus brings in the kingdom that belongs to the LORD.

books.name: Jonah
books.who: Unknown; about Jonah son of Amittai
books.big: A prophet runs from God, is swallowed by a fish, and sulks when God shows mercy to Israel's enemies.
books.jesus: Jesus points to "the sign of Jonah": three days and nights, then resurrection (Matthew 12:40).

books.name: Micah
books.big: Judgment on corruption, and hope of a ruler from Bethlehem. "Do justice, love mercy, walk humbly with your God."
books.jesus: Micah 5:2 names Bethlehem as the birthplace of the coming ruler: Jesus.

books.name: Nahum
books.big: God will judge Nineveh, the cruel capital of Assyria.
books.jesus: God's justice against evil is fully dealt with at the cross and Jesus' return.

books.name: Habakkuk
books.big: A prophet asks God hard questions about evil and learns to trust: "The righteous shall live by faith."
books.jesus: Paul builds the gospel on Habakkuk 2:4 (Romans 1:17).

books.name: Zephaniah
books.big: The Day of the LORD is near, but God will save a humble remnant and rejoice over them with singing.
books.jesus: Jesus is the King in the midst of his people who removes judgment.

books.name: Haggai
books.big: The returned exiles have neglected God's house; "consider your ways" and rebuild.
books.jesus: God promises to fill the house with glory and shake the nations, fulfilled when Jesus comes to the temple.

books.name: Zechariah
books.big: Visions and promises to encourage the builders: God will return, and a humble King will come.
books.jesus: Jesus rides into Jerusalem on a donkey (9:9) and is the pierced one (12:10) and the struck shepherd (13:7).

books.name: Malachi
books.big: God confronts half-hearted worship, broken marriages and robbing God, and promises a messenger to prepare the way.
books.jesus: John the Baptist is the messenger, and Jesus is the Lord who suddenly comes to his temple (3:1).

books.name: Matthew
books.who: Matthew (Levi), a former tax collector and one of the twelve apostles
books.when: Written around AD 60s for Jewish readers
books.big: Jesus is the promised Messiah, the King of the Jews, who fulfills the Old Testament and teaches what life in God's kingdom looks like.
books.jesus: Every chapter. Matthew keeps saying "this was to fulfill what was spoken by the prophet."

books.name: Mark
books.who: John Mark, based on Peter's preaching
books.big: Fast-moving: Jesus is the Son of God who came "not to be served but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many."
books.jesus: The whole book drives toward the cross and the empty tomb.

books.name: Luke
books.who: Luke, a doctor and Paul's companion
books.when: Around AD 60, carefully researched for Theophilus
books.big: An orderly account of Jesus, the Savior of the world, who seeks and saves the lost, outsiders, women, the poor and sinners.
books.jesus: Luke shows Jesus fulfilling "everything written about me in the Law, the Prophets and the Psalms" (24:44).

books.name: John
books.big: Written "so that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that by believing you may have life in his name."
books.jesus: Jesus' "I am" sayings: bread of life, light of the world, good shepherd, the resurrection and the life, the way, truth and life.

books.name: Acts
books.big: The risen Jesus sends his Spirit, and the gospel spreads from Jerusalem to Judea, Samaria and the ends of the earth through Peter, Paul and ordinary believers.
books.jesus: Jesus keeps working from heaven through his Spirit and his church.

books.name: Romans
books.when: Written from Corinth around AD 57 to the church in Rome
books.big: The gospel explained: everyone has sinned, and God makes sinners right with him by grace through faith in Jesus, then transforms how they live.
books.jesus: Jesus is the center: "There is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus" (8:1).

books.name: 1 Corinthians
books.when: Written from Ephesus around AD 55 to a messy church in Corinth
books.big: Paul tackles division, sexual sin, lawsuits, worship and spiritual gifts, and points to love and the resurrection.
books.jesus: "Christ crucified" (1:23) and Christ risen (15) answer every problem.

books.name: 2 Corinthians
books.when: Around AD 56, after a painful conflict with Corinth
books.big: Paul defends his ministry and shows that God's power shows up in weakness.
books.jesus: "God made him who had no sin to be sin for us, so that in him we might become the righteousness of God" (5:21).

books.name: Galatians
books.when: Around AD 48-55, to churches in Galatia
books.big: Don't add law-keeping to the gospel; we are justified by faith in Christ and set free to walk by the Spirit.
books.jesus: "I have been crucified with Christ… Christ lives in me" (2:20).

books.name: Ephesians
books.big: Everything God has given us in Christ (chapters 1-3), and how to live it out (4-6): unity, new life, family and spiritual battle.
books.jesus: God's plan is to unite all things in Christ (1:10).

books.name: Philippians
books.big: A thank-you letter full of joy in hard circumstances: "to live is Christ and to die is gain."
books.jesus: The hymn of 2:5-11: Jesus humbled himself to the cross and is exalted above every name.

books.name: Colossians
books.big: Jesus is supreme over everything, so you don't need anything added to him.
books.jesus: "He is the image of the invisible God… in him all things hold together" (1:15-17).

books.name: 1 Thessalonians
books.when: From Corinth around AD 50-51, one of his earliest letters
books.big: Encouragement to a young persecuted church: keep growing, live holy, and have hope in Jesus' return.
books.jesus: The Lord himself will come down from heaven (4:16).

books.name: 2 Thessalonians
books.big: The Day of the Lord hasn't come yet; stand firm and keep working.
books.jesus: Jesus will return and overcome evil.

books.name: 1 Timothy
books.when: Around AD 62-64, to his young co-worker Timothy in Ephesus
books.big: How to lead a church: guard sound teaching, pray, appoint qualified leaders and fight the good fight.
books.jesus: "Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, of whom I am the worst" (1:15).

books.name: 2 Timothy
books.who: Paul, from prison shortly before his death
books.big: Paul's last letter: guard the gospel, endure hardship like a soldier, and preach the word.
books.jesus: "Remember Jesus Christ, risen from the dead" (2:8).

books.name: Titus
books.when: Around AD 63, to Titus in Crete
books.big: Appoint good leaders and teach believers to live godly lives because of God's grace.
books.jesus: "The grace of God has appeared… our great God and Savior Jesus Christ" (2:11-13).

books.name: Philemon
books.big: Paul asks Philemon to welcome back his runaway slave Onesimus as a brother.
books.jesus: Paul offering to pay Onesimus's debt pictures what Jesus does for us.

books.name: Hebrews
books.when: Before AD 70, to Jewish Christians tempted to turn back
books.big: Jesus is better: better than angels, Moses, the priests and the sacrifices. So hold on and don't drift.
books.jesus: Jesus is the great high priest and the once-for-all sacrifice.

books.name: James
books.when: Around AD 45-50, one of the earliest New Testament books
books.big: Real faith shows up in real life: trials, speech, favoritism, money and humility.
books.jesus: James echoes Jesus' Sermon on the Mount throughout.

books.name: 1 Peter
books.big: You have a living hope; live as holy strangers in this world and endure suffering like Jesus did.
books.jesus: "He himself bore our sins in his body on the tree" (2:24).

books.name: 2 Peter
books.big: Grow in godliness, reject false teachers, and remember Jesus will return.
books.jesus: Peter was an eyewitness of Jesus' majesty (1:16).

books.name: 1 John
books.big: How to know you have eternal life: believe in Jesus, obey his commands and love one another. "God is love."
books.jesus: "The blood of Jesus his Son cleanses us from all sin" (1:7).

books.name: 2 John
books.big: Walk in truth and love, and don't welcome false teachers.
books.jesus: Confessing that Jesus came in the flesh is the test of truth.

books.name: 3 John
books.big: Praise for Gaius's hospitality and a warning about Diotrephes.
books.jesus: Faithful believers support those who go out "for the sake of the Name."

books.name: Jude
books.big: Contend for the faith against false teachers, and keep yourselves in God's love.
books.jesus: "To him who is able to keep you from stumbling" (24).

books.name: Revelation
books.big: A vision of the risen Jesus, the battle behind history, God's judgment on evil, and the new heaven and new earth.
books.jesus: Jesus is the Lamb who was slain, the King of kings, who says "I am making all things new."

items.title: Creation and fall
items.label: Beginning
items.text: God creates a good world and humanity in his image. Adam and Eve rebel, and sin and death enter. God promises a descendant who will crush the serpent.

items.title: The flood and Babel
items.label: Early history
items.text: Humanity grows violent. God judges with the flood, saves Noah and covenants with creation. Babel shows human pride scattered.

items.title: The patriarchs
items.label: c. 2000–1800 BC
items.text: God calls Abraham and promises land, offspring and blessing for all nations. The promise passes to Isaac, Jacob and Joseph.

items.title: Exodus and Sinai
items.label: c. 1446 BC (some date c. 1260 BC)
items.text: God rescues Israel from Egypt through Moses, gives the law at Sinai and dwells among them in the tabernacle.

items.title: Conquest and judges
items.label: c. 1400–1050 BC
items.text: Joshua leads Israel into Canaan. Israel cycles through sin, oppression, crying out and rescue under the judges.

items.title: The kingdom
items.label: c. 1050–930 BC
items.text: Saul, David and Solomon reign. God promises David an eternal throne. Solomon builds the temple.

items.title: Divided kingdom
items.label: 930–586 BC
items.text: Israel splits into north (Israel) and south (Judah). Prophets call both to return. Assyria conquers the north (722 BC).

items.title: Exile
items.label: 586–538 BC
items.text: Babylon destroys Jerusalem and the temple. Daniel and Ezekiel minister in exile. God promises a new covenant.

items.title: Return
items.label: 538–430 BC
items.text: Persia allows the Jews to return. The temple and walls are rebuilt under Zerubbabel, Ezra and Nehemiah.

items.title: Between the testaments
items.label: 430–5 BC
items.text: Around 400 years of no new canonical prophecy. Greek then Roman rule. Synagogues and expectation for the Messiah grow.

items.title: Jesus
items.label: c. 5 BC–AD 30/33
items.text: The Son of God becomes man, proclaims the kingdom, dies for sin and rises from the dead.

items.title: The church
items.label: AD 30–95
items.text: The Spirit comes at Pentecost. The gospel spreads from Jerusalem to Rome. The apostles write the New Testament.

items.title: New creation
items.label: Future
items.text: Christ returns, judges the world and makes all things new. God dwells with his people forever.

items.title: Noah
items.label: Genesis 9
items.text: God promises never again to destroy the earth by flood. Sign: the rainbow.

items.title: Abraham
items.label: Genesis 12, 15, 17
items.text: God promises land, descendants and blessing to all nations through Abraham’s offspring. Sign: circumcision.

items.title: Moses (Sinai)
items.label: Exodus 19–24
items.text: God makes Israel his treasured people and gives his law. Sign: the Sabbath.

items.title: David
items.label: 2 Samuel 7
items.text: God promises David a son whose throne will last forever.

items.title: The new covenant
items.label: Jeremiah 31; Luke 22
items.text: God promises to write his law on hearts and forgive sin forever. Jesus inaugurates it with his blood.

items.title: Offspring of the woman
items.label: Genesis 3:15
items.text: A descendant will crush the serpent.

items.title: Blessing to the nations
items.label: Genesis 22:18
items.text: All nations blessed through Abraham’s offspring.

items.title: Born in Bethlehem
items.label: Micah 5:2
items.text: A ruler from Bethlehem.

items.title: Son of David
items.label: Isaiah 9:6–7
items.text: A child on David’s throne forever.

items.title: Born of a virgin
items.label: Isaiah 7:14
items.text: A sign: Immanuel.

items.title: Riding on a donkey
items.label: Zechariah 9:9
items.text: The humble king comes.

items.title: The suffering servant
items.label: Isaiah 53
items.text: Pierced for our transgressions.

items.title: Forsaken
items.label: Psalm 22
items.text: My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?

items.title: Not abandoned to the grave
items.label: Psalm 16:10
items.text: The Holy One will not see decay.

bible.title: How to Read Each Kind of Book

items.title: Law
items.label: Genesis–Deuteronomy
items.text: Story and instruction. Ask what it shows about God’s holiness and how Christ fulfills it.

items.title: History
items.label: Joshua–Esther, Acts
items.text: True stories of God’s faithfulness. Not every action described is approved.

items.title: Poetry and wisdom
items.label: Job–Song of Songs
items.text: Feel, pray and ponder. Proverbs are general principles, not promises.

items.title: Prophets
items.label: Isaiah–Malachi
items.text: God’s messengers calling people back to covenant, with judgment and hope.

items.title: Gospels
items.label: Matthew–John
items.text: Four eyewitness-based portraits of Jesus.

items.title: Letters
items.label: Romans–Jude
items.text: Written to real churches. Read the whole letter and its situation.

items.title: Apocalyptic
items.label: Daniel, Revelation
items.text: Symbolic visions. Main point: God wins and Christ reigns.

items.title: Passover lamb
items.label: Exodus 12 → 1 Corinthians 5:7
items.text: Christ our Passover lamb has been sacrificed.

items.title: Bronze serpent
items.label: Numbers 21 → John 3:14
items.text: As the serpent was lifted up, so the Son of Man.

items.title: Manna
items.label: Exodus 16 → John 6
items.text: Jesus is the bread of life.

items.title: Temple
items.label: 1 Kings 8 → John 2:19–21
items.text: Jesus is where God dwells with man.

items.title: Jonah
items.label: Jonah 1 → Matthew 12:40
items.text: Three days and three nights.

items.title: Adam
items.label: Genesis 3 → Romans 5
items.text: Death through one man, life through one man.

manhood.title: Identity in Christ

refs.label: 2 Corinthians 5:17
refs.t: Therefore if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old things have passed away. Behold, all things have become new.

refs.label: Galatians 2:20
refs.t: I have been crucified with Christ, and it is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me. That life which I now live in the flesh, I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me, and gave himself up for me.

refs.label: Ephesians 2:8–10
refs.t: for by grace you have been saved through faith, and that not of yourselves; it is the gift of God, not of works, that no one would boast. For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared before that we would walk in them.

refs.label: 1 John 3:1
refs.t: See how great a love the Father has given to us, that we should be called children of God! For this cause the world doesn’t know us, because it didn’t know him.

manhood.summary: Before you are a husband, father, worker or leader, you are a son of God through Christ.
practice: Write down the three things you most often lean on for your sense of worth.
Read Ephesians 1 and list every phrase that begins with "in him" or "in Christ."
ask: Where do you feel most like a failure, and what does God say about you there?
What would change this week if you believed your worth was settled?
body: Most men build their identity on what they produce: income, title, strength, reputation. When those are shaken, the man is shaken. Scripture gives a different foundation. In Christ you are a new creation, saved by grace and not by works, and created for good works God prepared in advance.

This does not make a man passive. It frees him. A man who knows he is loved and accepted in Christ can take risks for the good of others, admit failure without being crushed and serve without needing applause.

manhood.title: The Husband

refs.label: Ephesians 5:25–33
refs.t: Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the assembly, and gave himself up for it; that he might sanctify it, having cleansed it by the washing of water with the word, that he might present the assembly to himself gloriously, not having spot or wrinkle or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without defect. Even so husbands also ought to love their own wives as their own bodies. He who loves his own wife loves himself. For no man ever hated his own flesh; but nourishes and cherishes it, even as the Lord also does the assembly; because we are members of his body, of his flesh and bones. “For this cause a man will leave his father and mother, and will be joined to his wife. The two will become one flesh.” This mystery is great, but I speak concerning Christ and of the assembly. Nevertheless each of you must also love his own wife even as himself; and let the wife see that she respects her husband.

refs.label: 1 Peter 3:7
refs.t: You husbands, in the same way, live with your wives according to knowledge, giving honor to the woman, as to the weaker vessel, as also being joint heirs of the grace of life, that your prayers may not be hindered.

refs.label: Colossians 3:19
refs.t: Husbands, love your wives, and don’t be bitter against them.

refs.label: Genesis 2:24
refs.t: Therefore a man will leave his father and his mother, and will join with his wife, and they will be one flesh.

manhood.summary: A husband loves his wife the way Christ loves the church: sacrificially, faithfully and with understanding.
practice: Ask your wife: "What is one thing I could do this week that would make you feel loved?" Then do it.
Pray with your wife for two minutes, even if it feels awkward.
ask: Where are you asking your wife to serve you more than you serve her?
What does "understanding" your wife require of you right now?
body: Paul’s command to husbands is not "be in charge." It is "love your wife as Christ loved the church and gave himself up for her." The measure of a husband’s leadership is the cross. Peter adds that husbands should live with their wives in an understanding way and honor them, so that their prayers will not be hindered.

Biblical headship is responsibility, not privilege. It means going first in repentance, prayer, forgiveness and service. It means protecting your wife’s heart, guarding your eyes and keeping your promises when feelings fade.

manhood.title: The Father

refs.label: Ephesians 6:4
refs.t: You fathers, don’t provoke your children to wrath, but nurture them in the discipline and instruction of the Lord.

refs.label: Deuteronomy 6:4–9
refs.t: Hear, Israel: Yahweh is our God. Yahweh is one. You shall love Yahweh your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your might. These words, which I command you today, shall be on your heart; and you shall teach them diligently to your children, and shall talk of them when you sit in your house, and when you walk by the way, and when you lie down, and when you rise up. You shall bind them for a sign on your hand, and they shall be for frontlets between your eyes. You shall write them on the door posts of your house and on your gates.

refs.label: Psalms 103:13
refs.t: Like a father has compassion on his children, so Yahweh has compassion on those who fear him.

refs.label: Proverbs 22:6
refs.t: Train up a child in the way he should go, and when he is old he will not depart from it.

manhood.summary: Fathers reflect the heavenly Father by teaching, disciplining with patience and being present.
practice: Bless each child this week by name, out loud, with a specific trait you see God growing in them.
Put the phone away for the first 20 minutes after you get home.
ask: What are your kids learning about God from how you treat them?
Where do you tend to provoke rather than instruct?
body: Scripture calls fathers to bring up children in the discipline and instruction of the Lord and not to provoke them to anger. Deuteronomy 6 pictures faith taught along the way: at the table, on the road, at bedtime and in the morning.

Children learn what a father values by where he spends his attention. The most powerful lessons are rarely lectures. They are a father who admits wrong, prays out loud, keeps his word and delights in his kids.

manhood.title: Integrity

refs.label: Proverbs 10:9
refs.t: He who walks blamelessly walks surely, but he who perverts his ways will be found out.

refs.label: Psalms 15:1–5
refs.t: Yahweh, who shall dwell in your sanctuary? Who shall live on your holy hill? He who walks blamelessly and does what is right, and speaks truth in his heart; he who doesn’t slander with his tongue, nor does evil to his friend, nor casts slurs against his fellow man; in whose eyes a vile man is despised, but who honors those who fear Yahweh; he who keeps an oath even when it hurts, and doesn’t change; he who doesn’t lend out his money for usury, nor take a bribe against the innocent. He who does these things shall never be shaken.

refs.label: Matthew 5:37
refs.t: But let your ‘Yes’ be ‘Yes’ and your ‘No’ be ‘No.’ Whatever is more than these is of the evil one.

refs.label: Proverbs 11:3
refs.t: The integrity of the upright shall guide them, but the perverseness of the treacherous shall destroy them.

manhood.summary: Integrity means being the same man in private as in public, and keeping your word.
practice: Identify one place where your private life does not match your public life, and tell a brother.
Keep every small promise you make this week.
ask: Who would be surprised if they saw your whole week?
What promise have you not kept?
body: The man who walks in integrity walks securely. Psalm 15 describes the person who may dwell with God: he speaks truth in his heart and keeps his oath even when it hurts. Jesus says simply: let your yes be yes and your no be no.
Integrity is built in small moments: the hours you bill, the corners you do not cut, the jokes you do not tell, the screen you turn off when no one is watching.

manhood.title: Sexual Purity

refs.label: 1 Thessalonians 4:3–8
refs.t: For this is the will of God: your sanctification, that you abstain from sexual immorality, that each one of you know how to control his own body in sanctification and honor, not in the passion of lust, even as the Gentiles who don’t know God, that no one should take advantage of and wrong a brother or sister in this matter; because the Lord is an avenger in all these things, as also we forewarned you and testified. For God called us not for uncleanness, but in sanctification. Therefore he who rejects this doesn’t reject man, but God, who has also given his Holy Spirit to you.

refs.label: Matthew 5:27–30
refs.t: “You have heard that it was said, ‘You shall not commit adultery;’ but I tell you that everyone who gazes at a woman to lust after her has committed adultery with her already in his heart. If your right eye causes you to stumble, pluck it out and throw it away from you. For it is more profitable for you that one of your members should perish, than for your whole body to be cast into Gehenna. If your right hand causes you to stumble, cut it off, and throw it away from you. For it is more profitable for you that one of your members should perish, than for your whole body to be cast into Gehenna.

refs.label: 1 Corinthians 6:18–20
refs.t: Flee sexual immorality! “Every sin that a man does is outside the body,” but he who commits sexual immorality sins against his own body. Or don’t you know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit who is in you, whom you have from God? You are not your own, for you were bought with a price. Therefore glorify God in your body and in your spirit, which are God’s.

refs.label: Job 31:1
refs.t: “I made a covenant with my eyes, how then should I look lustfully at a young woman?

refs.label: 1 John 1:9
refs.t: If we confess our sins, he is faithful and righteous to forgive us the sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.

manhood.summary: God calls men to sexual purity, offers full forgiveness and gives power to fight.
practice: Install accountability software or remove the app you know is a problem.
Tell one brother the truth about your struggle this week.
ask: When are you most vulnerable to temptation (time, place, mood)?
What is one barrier you could put in place today?
body: Jesus raised the standard: lust in the heart is adultery. Paul tells believers to flee sexual immorality because the body is a temple of the Holy Spirit. Job made a covenant with his eyes.

Shame says hide. The gospel says confess. If we confess our sins, God is faithful and just to forgive. Lasting freedom usually involves honest confession to a trusted brother, practical barriers (filters, device rules, changed routines) and replacing secrecy with light.

manhood.title: Work and Calling

refs.label: Colossians 3:23–24
refs.t: And whatever you do, work heartily, as for the Lord, and not for men, knowing that from the Lord you will receive the reward of the inheritance; for you serve the Lord Christ.

refs.label: Genesis 2:15
refs.t: Yahweh God took the man, and put him into the garden of Eden to cultivate and keep it.

refs.label: Proverbs 6:6–11
refs.t: Go to the ant, you sluggard. Consider her ways, and be wise; which having no chief, overseer, or ruler, provides her bread in the summer, and gathers her food in the harvest. How long will you sleep, sluggard? When will you arise out of your sleep? A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to sleep: so your poverty will come as a robber, and your scarcity as an armed man.

refs.label: 2 Thessalonians 3:10–12
refs.t: For even when we were with you, we commanded you this: “If anyone is not willing to work, don’t let him eat.” For we hear of some who walk among you in rebellion, who don’t work at all, but are busybodies. Now those who are that way, we command and exhort in the Lord Jesus Christ, that they work with quietness and eat their own bread.

refs.label: Ecclesiastes 9:10
refs.t: Whatever your hand finds to do, do it with your might; for there is no work, nor plan, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in Sheol, where you are going.

manhood.summary: Work is a gift from God, done for the Lord and not for men.
practice: Begin each workday this week with a one-sentence prayer offering your work to God.
Do one task with excellence that no one will notice.
ask: Is work more of an idol or more of a burden for you right now?
How could your coworkers see Christ in how you work?
body: Before sin entered the world, God put Adam in the garden to work it and keep it. Work is not a curse; the curse made it toilsome. Paul tells believers to work heartily as for the Lord, knowing their reward comes from him.
A Christian man works with diligence, honesty and excellence. He refuses to make work an idol and refuses to be lazy. He sees his job as a place to serve others and to show the character of Christ.

manhood.title: Money and Stewardship

refs.label: Matthew 6:19–24
refs.t: “Don’t lay up treasures for yourselves on the earth, where moth and rust consume, and where thieves break through and steal; but lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust consume, and where thieves don’t break through and steal; for where your treasure is, there your heart will be also. “The lamp of the body is the eye. If therefore your eye is sound, your whole body will be full of light. But if your eye is evil, your whole body will be full of darkness. If therefore the light that is in you is darkness, how great is the darkness! “No one can serve two masters, for either he will hate the one and love the other; or else he will be devoted to one and despise the other. You can’t serve both God and Mammon.

refs.label: 1 Timothy 6:6–10
refs.t: But godliness with contentment is great gain. For we brought nothing into the world, and we certainly can’t carry anything out. But having food and clothing, we will be content with that. But those who are determined to be rich fall into a temptation, a snare, and many foolish and harmful lusts, such as drown men in ruin and destruction. For the love of money is a root of all kinds of evil. Some have been led astray from the faith in their greed, and have pierced themselves through with many sorrows.

refs.label: Proverbs 3:9–10
refs.t: Honor Yahweh with your substance, with the first fruits of all your increase: so your barns will be filled with plenty, and your vats will overflow with new wine.

refs.label: 2 Corinthians 9:6–8
refs.t: Remember this: he who sows sparingly will also reap sparingly. He who sows bountifully will also reap bountifully. Let each man give according as he has determined in his heart, not grudgingly or under compulsion, for God loves a cheerful giver. And God is able to make all grace abound to you, that you, always having all sufficiency in everything, may abound to every good work.

refs.label: Luke 16:10–11
refs.t: He who is faithful in a very little is faithful also in much. He who is dishonest in a very little is also dishonest in much. If therefore you have not been faithful in the unrighteous mammon, who will commit to your trust the true riches?

manhood.summary: Everything belongs to God. A steward manages it faithfully, gives generously and avoids the love of money.
practice: Look at last month’s spending with your wife or a trusted friend.
Set a giving amount you will give first, before anything else.
ask: Where does money compete with God for your trust?
What would contentment look like for you this year?
body: Jesus said you cannot serve both God and money. Paul warns that the love of money is a root of all kinds of evil and commends godliness with contentment. Scripture also calls us to honor the Lord with the first of our income and to give cheerfully.
Faithful stewardship is practical: living below your means, avoiding debt that enslaves, providing for your household, saving wisely and giving first.

manhood.title: Anger and Self-Control

refs.label: James 1:19–20
refs.t: So, then, my beloved brothers, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, and slow to anger; for the anger of man doesn’t produce the righteousness of God.

refs.label: Ephesians 4:26–27
refs.t: “Be angry, and don’t sin.” Don’t let the sun go down on your wrath, and don’t give place to the devil.

refs.label: Proverbs 16:32
refs.t: One who is slow to anger is better than the mighty; one who rules his spirit, than he who takes a city.

refs.label: Proverbs 15:1
refs.t: A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.

refs.label: Galatians 5:22–23
refs.t: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faith, gentleness, and self-control. Against such things there is no law.

manhood.summary: Be quick to hear, slow to speak and slow to anger. Self-control is fruit of the Spirit.
practice: When you feel anger rise, pause and breathe before you speak.
Ask your family when your anger hurts them most, and listen without defending.
ask: What usually sits underneath your anger: fear, pride, exhaustion?
Who needs an apology from you?
body: Not all anger is sin. Jesus was angry at injustice. But James warns that human anger does not produce the righteousness of God. Paul says do not let the sun go down on your anger, which gives the devil a foothold.
Ruling your own spirit is better than conquering a city. Self-control is not white-knuckle effort alone; it is fruit the Spirit grows as we walk with him.

manhood.title: Servant Leadership

refs.label: Mark 10:42–45
refs.t: Jesus summoned them, and said to them, “You know that they who are recognized as rulers over the nations lord it over them, and their great ones exercise authority over them. But it shall not be so among you, but whoever wants to become great among you shall be your servant. Whoever of you wants to become first among you, shall be bondservant of all. For the Son of Man also came not to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.”

refs.label: John 13:12–17
refs.t: So when he had washed their feet, put his outer garment back on, and sat down again, he said to them, “Do you know what I have done to you? You call me, ‘Teacher’ and ‘Lord.’ You say so correctly, for so I am. If I then, the Lord and the Teacher, have washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another’s feet. For I have given you an example, that you should also do as I have done to you. Most certainly I tell you, a servant is not greater than his lord, neither is one who is sent greater than he who sent him. If you know these things, blessed are you if you do them.

refs.label: 1 Peter 5:2–3
refs.t: Shepherd the flock of God which is among you, exercising the oversight, not under compulsion, but voluntarily, not for dishonest gain, but willingly; not as lording it over those entrusted to you, but making yourselves examples to the flock.

refs.label: Philippians 2:3–8
refs.t: doing nothing through rivalry or through conceit, but in humility, each counting others better than himself; each of you not just looking to his own things, but each of you also to the things of others. Have this in your mind, which was also in Christ Jesus, who, existing in the form of God, didn’t consider equality with God a thing to be grasped, but emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, being made in the likeness of men. And being found in human form, he humbled himself, becoming obedient to the point of death, yes, the death of the cross.

manhood.summary: In the kingdom, the greatest is the servant of all.
practice: Do one unseen act of service for someone you lead.
Ask someone under your leadership: "How could I serve you better?"
ask: Where do you use your position to be served?
Who is following your example, for better or worse?
body: Jesus redefined leadership: whoever wants to be great must be the servant of all, for the Son of Man came not to be served but to serve. He washed his disciples’ feet and told them to do the same.
A servant leader goes first, takes responsibility, gives credit away, listens before deciding and uses authority to build others up, not to protect himself.

manhood.title: Courage

refs.label: Joshua 1:6–9
refs.t: “Be strong and courageous; for you shall cause this people to inherit the land which I swore to their fathers to give them. Only be strong and very courageous. Be careful to observe to do according to all the law which Moses my servant commanded you. Don’t turn from it to the right hand or to the left, that you may have good success wherever you go. This book of the law shall not depart from your mouth, but you shall meditate on it day and night, that you may observe to do according to all that is written in it; for then you shall make your way prosperous, and then you shall have good success. Haven’t I commanded you? Be strong and courageous. Don’t be afraid. Don’t be dismayed, for Yahweh your God is with you wherever you go.”

refs.label: 1 Corinthians 16:13–14
refs.t: Watch! Stand firm in the faith! Be courageous! Be strong! Let all that you do be done in love.

refs.label: 2 Timothy 1:7
refs.t: For God didn’t give us a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and self-control.

refs.label: Psalms 27:1
refs.t: Yahweh is my light and my salvation. Whom shall I fear? Yahweh is the strength of my life. Of whom shall I be afraid?

manhood.summary: Biblical courage is not the absence of fear but obedience because God is with you.
practice: Have the conversation you have been avoiding.
Memorize Joshua 1:9.
ask: What fear is keeping you from obedience right now?
Where do you need courage combined with love?
body: God told Joshua three times to be strong and courageous, and grounded it in a promise: the Lord your God is with you wherever you go. Paul tells the church to stand firm, act like men, be strong, and let all be done in love.
Courage looks like telling the truth, having the hard conversation, admitting sin, standing for the vulnerable and sharing your faith.

manhood.title: Brotherhood and Friendship

refs.label: Proverbs 27:17
refs.t: Iron sharpens iron; so a man sharpens his friend’s countenance.

refs.label: Ecclesiastes 4:9–12
refs.t: Two are better than one, because they have a good reward for their labor. For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow; but woe to him who is alone when he falls, and doesn’t have another to lift him up. Again, if two lie together, then they have warmth; but how can one keep warm alone? If a man prevails against one who is alone, two shall withstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.

refs.label: Hebrews 10:24–25
refs.t: Let’s consider how to provoke one another to love and good works, not forsaking our own assembling together, as the custom of some is, but exhorting one another, and so much the more as you see the Day approaching.

refs.label: James 5:16
refs.t: Confess your offenses to one another, and pray for one another, that you may be healed. The insistent prayer of a righteous person is powerfully effective.

refs.label: Proverbs 18:24
refs.t: A man of many companions may be ruined, but there is a friend who sticks closer than a brother.

manhood.summary: Iron sharpens iron. Men need brothers who know them and push them toward Christ.
practice: Invite one man to coffee this week with no agenda but to know him.
Share one real struggle with your crew.
ask: Who knows the real you?
What keeps you from letting other men in?
body: Many men have coworkers and acquaintances but no one who truly knows them. Scripture says two are better than one, and a threefold cord is not quickly broken. Hebrews tells believers not to give up meeting together but to stir one another up to love and good works.
Real brotherhood requires honesty, regular time together, confession and prayer for one another.

manhood.title: A Man of Prayer

refs.label: Matthew 6:5–13
refs.t: “When you pray, you shall not be as the hypocrites, for they love to stand and pray in the synagogues and in the corners of the streets, that they may be seen by men. Most certainly, I tell you, they have received their reward. But you, when you pray, enter into your inner room, and having shut your door, pray to your Father who is in secret, and your Father who sees in secret will reward you openly. In praying, don’t use vain repetitions, as the Gentiles do; for they think that they will be heard for their much speaking. Therefore don’t be like them, for your Father knows what things you need, before you ask him. Pray like this: ‘Our Father in heaven, may your name be kept holy. Let your Kingdom come. Let your will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us today our daily bread. Forgive us our debts, as we also forgive our debtors. Bring us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one. For yours is the Kingdom, the power, and the glory forever. Amen.’

refs.label: 1 Thessalonians 5:16–18
refs.t: Always rejoice. Pray without ceasing. In everything give thanks, for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus toward you.

refs.label: Philippians 4:6–7
refs.t: In nothing be anxious, but in everything, by prayer and petition with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God. And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your thoughts in Christ Jesus.

refs.label: Luke 18:1
refs.t: He also spoke a parable to them that they must always pray, and not give up,

manhood.summary: Prayer is not a performance. It is a son talking with his Father.
practice: Pray through the Lord’s Prayer slowly each day this week.
Keep a list of prayer requests and note answers.
ask: What keeps you from praying?
What would you ask God for if you really believed he listens?
body: Jesus taught his disciples to pray to "Our Father," and he often withdrew to lonely places to pray. Paul tells believers to pray without ceasing and to bring every anxiety to God with thanksgiving.
Many men feel awkward praying. Start simple: thank God, confess sin, ask for help, pray for others. Use the Lord’s Prayer as a framework. Consistency matters more than eloquence.

manhood.title: Suffering and Perseverance

refs.label: Romans 5:3–5
refs.t: Not only this, but we also rejoice in our sufferings, knowing that suffering produces perseverance; and perseverance, proven character; and proven character, hope: and hope doesn’t disappoint us, because God’s love has been poured into our hearts through the Holy Spirit who was given to us.

refs.label: James 1:2–4
refs.t: Count it all joy, my brothers, when you fall into various temptations, knowing that the testing of your faith produces endurance. Let endurance have its perfect work, that you may be perfect and complete, lacking in nothing.

refs.label: 2 Corinthians 4:16–18
refs.t: Therefore we don’t faint, but though our outward man is decaying, yet our inward man is renewed day by day. For our light affliction, which is for the moment, works for us more and more exceedingly an eternal weight of glory, while we don’t look at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen. For the things which are seen are temporal, but the things which are not seen are eternal.

refs.label: 1 Peter 5:10
refs.t: But may the God of all grace, who called you to his eternal glory by Christ Jesus, after you have suffered a little while, perfect, establish, strengthen, and settle you.

manhood.summary: God uses trials to produce endurance, character and hope.
practice: Write an honest lament to God, using Psalm 13 as a model.
Reach out to one brother who is suffering.
ask: What trial are you in right now?
What might God be producing in you through it?
body: Christians are not promised an easy life. James says to count it joy when you face trials, because testing produces steadfastness. Paul says suffering produces endurance, endurance produces character and character produces hope.
Suffering is real and grief is not faithlessness. The Psalms are full of honest lament. God does not waste pain, and he is near the brokenhearted.

manhood.title: Legacy

refs.label: Psalms 78:4–7
refs.t: We will not hide them from their children, telling to the generation to come the praises of Yahweh, his strength, and his wondrous deeds that he has done. For he established a covenant in Jacob, and appointed a teaching in Israel, which he commanded our fathers, that they should make them known to their children; that the generation to come might know, even the children who should be born; who should arise and tell their children, that they might set their hope in God, and not forget God’s deeds, but keep his commandments,

refs.label: 2 Timothy 2:2
refs.t: The things which you have heard from me among many witnesses, commit the same things to faithful men, who will be able to teach others also.

refs.label: Proverbs 13:22
refs.t: A good man leaves an inheritance to his children’s children, but the wealth of the sinner is stored for the righteous.

refs.label: 2 Timothy 4:7–8
refs.t: I have fought the good fight. I have finished the course. I have kept the faith. From now on, the crown of righteousness is stored up for me, which the Lord, the righteous judge, will give to me on that day; and not to me only, but also to all those who have loved his appearing.

manhood.summary: A godly man lives for what outlasts him: faith passed to the next generation.
practice: Write a letter to your children or a younger man about what God has done in your life.
Choose one younger man to invest in this year.
ask: What will people remember about you?
Who are you discipling?
body: Psalm 78 calls one generation to tell the next about the works of the Lord so that they would set their hope in God. Paul told Timothy to entrust what he had learned to faithful men who would teach others.
Legacy is not mainly an inheritance of money. It is the faith, character and memories you leave in the people you love.

questions.title: Why does God allow suffering?

refs.label: Genesis 50:20
refs.t: As for you, you meant evil against me, but God meant it for good, to save many people alive, as is happening today.

refs.label: Romans 8:18–28
refs.t: For I consider that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which will be revealed toward us. For the creation waits with eager expectation for the children of God to be revealed. For the creation was subjected to vanity, not of its own will, but because of him who subjected it, in hope that the creation itself also will be delivered from the bondage of decay into the liberty of the glory of the children of God. For we know that the whole creation groans and travails in pain together until now. Not only so, but ourselves also, who have the first fruits of the Spirit, even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for adoption, the redemption of our body. For we were saved in hope, but hope that is seen is not hope. For who hopes for that which he sees? But if we hope for that which we don’t see, we wait for it with patience. In the same way, the Spirit also helps our weaknesses, for we don’t know how to pray as we ought. But the Spirit himself makes intercession for us with groanings which can’t be uttered. He who searches the hearts knows what is on the Spirit’s mind, because he makes intercession for the saints according to God. We know that all things work together for good for those who love God, for those who are called according to his purpose.

refs.label: Revelation 21:3–5
refs.t: I heard a loud voice out of heaven saying, “Behold, God’s dwelling is with people, and he will dwell with them, and they will be his people, and God himself will be with them as their God. He will wipe away every tear from their eyes. Death will be no more; neither will there be mourning, nor crying, nor pain, any more. The first things have passed away.” He who sits on the throne said, “Behold, I am making all things new.” He said, “Write, for these words of God are faithful and true.”

refs.label: Job 38:1–7
refs.t: Then Yahweh answered Job out of the whirlwind, “Who is this who darkens counsel by words without knowledge? Brace yourself like a man, for I will question you, then you answer me! “Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth? Declare, if you have understanding. Who determined its measures, if you know? Or who stretched the line on it? What were its foundations fastened on? Or who laid its cornerstone, when the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy?

refs.label: John 11:33–35
refs.t: When Jesus therefore saw her weeping, and the Jews weeping who came with her, he groaned in the spirit, and was troubled, and said, “Where have you laid him?” They told him, “Lord, come and see.” Jesus wept.

questions.summary: Scripture does not give one tidy answer, but it gives a God who suffers with us and promises to end suffering.
questions.views: Christians emphasize different aspects: God’s sovereignty over all things (Reformed), the reality of human free will (Arminian/Wesleyan) and the mystery of evil (many traditions). All affirm God is good and evil is real.
body: The Bible takes suffering seriously. It traces much of it to the fall: a world broken by sin, both our own and others’. It shows that God can bring good even out of evil done to us, as Joseph told his brothers. It promises a day when God will wipe away every tear.

The book of Job warns against easy explanations. God never tells Job why he suffered; he reveals himself. At the cross, God himself enters suffering. Jesus wept at Lazarus’ tomb even though he was about to raise him.

questions.title: Is Jesus the only way to God?

refs.label: John 14:6
refs.t: Jesus said to him, “I am the way, the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father, except through me.

refs.label: Acts 4:12
refs.t: There is salvation in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven that is given among men, by which we must be saved!”

refs.label: 1 Timothy 2:5–6
refs.t: For there is one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus, who gave himself as a ransom for all, the testimony in its own times,

refs.label: Romans 10:9–15
refs.t: that if you will confess with your mouth that Jesus is Lord, and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved. For with the heart, one believes resulting in righteousness; and with the mouth confession is made resulting in salvation. For the Scripture says, “Whoever believes in him will not be disappointed.” For there is no distinction between Jew and Greek; for the same Lord is Lord of all, and is rich to all who call on him. For, “Whoever will call on the name of the Lord will be saved.” How then will they call on him in whom they have not believed? How will they believe in him whom they have not heard? How will they hear without a preacher? And how will they preach unless they are sent? As it is written: “How beautiful are the feet of those who preach the Good News of peace, who bring glad tidings of good things!”

questions.summary: Jesus claimed to be the only way to the Father, and the apostles proclaimed salvation in his name alone.
questions.views: Christians agree salvation is through Christ alone. They differ on questions like the fate of those who never heard the gospel, and many leave that with a just and merciful God.
body: Jesus said, "I am the way, the truth and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me." Peter declared there is no other name under heaven by which we must be saved. This can sound narrow, but the invitation is wide: whoever calls on the name of the Lord will be saved.
Christianity is unique in that it says salvation is a gift, not an achievement. That is why it centers on a person, not a program.

questions.title: Can I trust the Bible?

refs.label: 2 Timothy 3:16–17
refs.t: Every Scripture is God-breathed and profitable for teaching, for reproof, for correction, and for instruction in righteousness, that each person who belongs to God may be complete, thoroughly equipped for every good work.

refs.label: 2 Peter 1:16–21
refs.t: For we didn’t follow cunningly devised fables when we made known to you the power and coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, but we were eyewitnesses of his majesty. For he received from God the Father honor and glory when the voice came to him from the Majestic Glory, “This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.” We heard this voice come out of heaven when we were with him on the holy mountain. We have the more sure word of prophecy; and you do well that you heed it, as to a lamp shining in a dark place, until the day dawns, and the morning star arises in your hearts: knowing this first, that no prophecy of Scripture is of private interpretation. For no prophecy ever came by the will of man: but holy men of God spoke, being moved by the Holy Spirit.

refs.label: Luke 1:1–4
refs.t: Since many have undertaken to set in order a narrative concerning those matters which have been fulfilled among us, even as those who from the beginning were eyewitnesses and servants of the word delivered them to us, it seemed good to me also, having traced the course of all things accurately from the first, to write to you in order, most excellent Theophilus; that you might know the certainty concerning the things in which you were instructed.

refs.label: Psalms 19:7–11
refs.t: Yahweh’s law is perfect, restoring the soul. Yahweh’s covenant is sure, making wise the simple. Yahweh’s precepts are right, rejoicing the heart. Yahweh’s commandment is pure, enlightening the eyes. The fear of Yahweh is clean, enduring forever. Yahweh’s ordinances are true, and righteous altogether. They are more to be desired than gold, yes, than much fine gold, sweeter also than honey and the extract of the honeycomb. Moreover your servant is warned by them. In keeping them there is great reward.

questions.summary: The Bible claims to be God-breathed, and it has strong historical and manuscript support.
questions.views: Christians hold differing views on how to describe inspiration (for example, inerrancy versus infallibility), and Protestants, Catholics and Orthodox recognize different numbers of Old Testament books.
body: Paul writes that all Scripture is breathed out by God and profitable for teaching and training. Peter says the apostles were eyewitnesses, not followers of clever myths. Luke says he carefully investigated everything.

Historically, the New Testament is attested by thousands of early manuscripts, far more than any other ancient work. Archaeology has confirmed many people and places it names. Differences among manuscripts are mostly minor and do not affect core doctrine.

questions.title: Why doesn’t God answer my prayers?

refs.label: Matthew 7:7–11
refs.t: “Ask, and it will be given you. Seek, and you will find. Knock, and it will be opened for you. For everyone who asks receives. He who seeks finds. To him who knocks it will be opened. Or who is there among you, who, if his son asks him for bread, will give him a stone? Or if he asks for a fish, who will give him a serpent? If you then, being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father who is in heaven give good things to those who ask him!

refs.label: 2 Corinthians 12:7–10
refs.t: By reason of the exceeding greatness of the revelations, that I should not be exalted excessively, a thorn in the flesh was given to me: a messenger of Satan to torment me, that I should not be exalted excessively. Concerning this thing, I begged the Lord three times that it might depart from me. He has said to me, “My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness.” Most gladly therefore I will rather glory in my weaknesses, that the power of Christ may rest on me. Therefore I take pleasure in weaknesses, in injuries, in necessities, in persecutions, and in distresses, for Christ’s sake. For when I am weak, then am I strong.

refs.label: James 4:2–3
refs.t: You lust, and don’t have. You murder and covet, and can’t obtain. You fight and make war. You don’t have, because you don’t ask. You ask, and don’t receive, because you ask with wrong motives, so that you may spend it on your pleasures.

refs.label: Luke 22:42
refs.t: saying, “Father, if you are willing, remove this cup from me. Nevertheless, not my will, but yours, be done.”

questions.summary: God hears every prayer. Sometimes the answer is yes, sometimes no, sometimes wait.
body: Jesus encourages persistent prayer and promises a good Father. Yet Paul asked three times for his thorn to be removed and God said, "My grace is sufficient for you." Jesus himself prayed "not my will but yours."
James also notes we sometimes ask with wrong motives. Silence can be a season of growth. Keep praying, keep a record and remember that God’s goal is to make us more like Christ.

questions.title: Is it wrong to doubt?

refs.label: Mark 9:24
refs.t: Immediately the father of the child cried out with tears, “I believe. Help my unbelief!”

refs.label: Jude 1:22
refs.t: On some have compassion, making a distinction,

refs.label: John 20:24–29
refs.t: But Thomas, one of the twelve, called Didymus, wasn’t with them when Jesus came. The other disciples therefore said to him, “We have seen the Lord!” But he said to them, “Unless I see in his hands the print of the nails, put my finger into the print of the nails, and put my hand into his side, I will not believe.” After eight days again his disciples were inside and Thomas was with them. Jesus came, the doors being locked, and stood in the middle, and said, “Peace be to you.” Then he said to Thomas, “Reach here your finger, and see my hands. Reach here your hand, and put it into my side. Don’t be unbelieving, but believing.” Thomas answered him, “My Lord and my God!” Jesus said to him, “Because you have seen me, you have believed. Blessed are those who have not seen, and have believed.”

refs.label: Psalms 73:1–28
refs.t: Surely God is good to Israel, to those who are pure in heart. But as for me, my feet were almost gone. My steps had nearly slipped. For I was envious of the arrogant, when I saw the prosperity of the wicked. For there are no struggles in their death, but their strength is firm. They are free from burdens of men, neither are they plagued like other men. Therefore pride is like a chain around their neck. Violence covers them like a garment. Their eyes bulge with fat. Their minds pass the limits of conceit. They scoff and speak with malice. In arrogance, they threaten oppression. They have set their mouth in the heavens. Their tongue walks through the earth. Therefore their people return to them, and they drink up waters of abundance. They say, “How does God know? Is there knowledge in the Most High?” Behold, these are the wicked. Being always at ease, they increase in riches. Surely I have cleansed my heart in vain, and washed my hands in innocence, For all day long I have been plagued, and punished every morning. If I had said, “I will speak thus”; behold, I would have betrayed the generation of your children. When I tried to understand this, it was too painful for me, until I entered God’s sanctuary, and considered their latter end. Surely you set them in slippery places. You throw them down to destruction. How they are suddenly destroyed! They are completely swept away with terrors. As a dream when one wakes up, so, Lord, when you awake, you will despise their fantasies. For my soul was grieved. I was embittered in my heart. I was so senseless and ignorant. I was a brute beast before you. Nevertheless, I am continually with you. You have held my right hand. You will guide me with your counsel, and afterward receive me to glory. Whom do I have in heaven? There is no one on earth whom I desire besides you. My flesh and my heart fails, but God is the strength of my heart and my portion forever. For, behold, those who are far from you shall perish. You have destroyed all those who are unfaithful to you. But it is good for me to come close to God. I have made the Lord Yahweh my refuge, that I may tell of all your works.

questions.summary: Doubt is not the opposite of faith. Unbelief that refuses to seek is.
body: A desperate father cried, "I believe; help my unbelief!" and Jesus healed his son. Jude tells believers to have mercy on those who doubt. Thomas doubted and Jesus met him with evidence.
Bring your doubts to God and to mature believers. Study, ask questions and keep obeying what you do know.

questions.title: What does the Bible say about hell?

refs.label: Matthew 25:31–46
refs.t: “But when the Son of Man comes in his glory, and all the holy angels with him, then he will sit on the throne of his glory. Before him all the nations will be gathered, and he will separate them one from another, as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats. He will set the sheep on his right hand, but the goats on the left. Then the King will tell those on his right hand, ‘Come, blessed of my Father, inherit the Kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world; for I was hungry, and you gave me food to eat. I was thirsty, and you gave me drink. I was a stranger, and you took me in. I was naked, and you clothed me. I was sick, and you visited me. I was in prison, and you came to me.’ “Then the righteous will answer him, saying, ‘Lord, when did we see you hungry, and feed you; or thirsty, and give you a drink? When did we see you as a stranger, and take you in; or naked, and clothe you? When did we see you sick, or in prison, and come to you?’ “The King will answer them, ‘Most certainly I tell you, because you did it to one of the least of these my brothers, you did it to me.’ Then he will say also to those on the left hand, ‘Depart from me, you cursed, into the eternal fire which is prepared for the devil and his angels; for I was hungry, and you didn’t give me food to eat; I was thirsty, and you gave me no drink; I was a stranger, and you didn’t take me in; naked, and you didn’t clothe me; sick, and in prison, and you didn’t visit me.’ “Then they will also answer, saying, ‘Lord, when did we see you hungry, or thirsty, or a stranger, or naked, or sick, or in prison, and didn’t help you?’ “Then he will answer them, saying, ‘Most certainly I tell you, because you didn’t do it to one of the least of these, you didn’t do it to me.’ These will go away into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life.”

refs.label: 2 Thessalonians 1:7–10
refs.t: and to give relief to you who are afflicted with us, when the Lord Jesus is revealed from heaven with his mighty angels in flaming fire, punishing those who don’t know God, and to those who don’t obey the Good News of our Lord Jesus, who will pay the penalty: eternal destruction from the face of the Lord and from the glory of his might, when he comes in that day to be glorified in his saints and to be admired among all those who have believed, because our testimony to you was believed.

refs.label: Revelation 20:11–15
refs.t: I saw a great white throne, and him who sat on it, from whose face the earth and the heaven fled away. There was found no place for them. I saw the dead, the great and the small, standing before the throne, and they opened books. Another book was opened, which is the book of life. The dead were judged out of the things which were written in the books, according to their works. The sea gave up the dead who were in it. Death and Hades gave up the dead who were in them. They were judged, each one according to his works. Death and Hades were thrown into the lake of fire. This is the second death, the lake of fire. If anyone was not found written in the book of life, he was cast into the lake of fire.

refs.label: 2 Peter 3:9
refs.t: The Lord is not slow concerning his promise, as some count slowness; but he is patient with us, not wishing that anyone should perish, but that all should come to repentance.

questions.summary: Jesus spoke of final judgment more than anyone else, and God desires that none perish.
questions.views: Most Christians historically have held to conscious eternal punishment. Some evangelicals hold to conditional immortality (annihilation). All affirm a real final judgment and urge people to Christ.
body: Jesus warned of judgment, of outer darkness and of eternal punishment. Scripture presents judgment as just, taking evil seriously. It also says God is patient, not wanting any to perish but all to reach repentance.

questions.title: Do faith and science conflict?

refs.label: Psalms 19:1–4
refs.t: The heavens declare the glory of God. The expanse shows his handiwork. Day after day they pour out speech, and night after night they display knowledge. There is no speech nor language, where their voice is not heard. Their voice has gone out through all the earth, their words to the end of the world. In them he has set a tent for the sun,

refs.label: Romans 1:20
refs.t: For the invisible things of him since the creation of the world are clearly seen, being perceived through the things that are made, even his everlasting power and divinity, that they may be without excuse.

refs.label: Genesis 1:1
refs.t: In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth.

refs.label: Colossians 1:16–17
refs.t: For by him all things were created in the heavens and on the earth, visible things and invisible things, whether thrones or dominions or principalities or powers. All things have been created through him and for him. He is before all things, and in him all things are held together.

questions.summary: The heavens declare the glory of God. Many founders of modern science were Christians.
questions.views: Christians hold different views on the age of the earth and how to read Genesis 1 (young-earth, old-earth, framework and evolutionary creation). All affirm God as Creator.
body: Scripture says creation reveals God’s power. Christians believe God made an orderly world that can be studied. Science answers how things work; Scripture answers who made them and why.

questions.title: Can a Christian keep sinning?

refs.label: Romans 6:1–14
refs.t: What shall we say then? Shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound? May it never be! We who died to sin, how could we live in it any longer? Or don’t you know that all we who were baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into his death? We were buried therefore with him through baptism into death, that just as Christ was raised from the dead through the glory of the Father, so we also might walk in newness of life. For if we have become united with him in the likeness of his death, we will also be part of his resurrection; knowing this, that our old man was crucified with him, that the body of sin might be done away with, so that we would no longer be in bondage to sin. For he who has died has been freed from sin. But if we died with Christ, we believe that we will also live with him; knowing that Christ, being raised from the dead, dies no more. Death no longer has dominion over him! For the death that he died, he died to sin one time; but the life that he lives, he lives to God. Thus consider yourselves also to be dead to sin, but alive to God in Christ Jesus our Lord. Therefore don’t let sin reign in your mortal body, that you should obey it in its lusts. Also, do not present your members to sin as instruments of unrighteousness, but present yourselves to God as alive from the dead, and your members as instruments of righteousness to God. For sin will not have dominion over you. For you are not under law, but under grace.

refs.label: 1 John 1:8–10
refs.t: If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us. If we confess our sins, he is faithful and righteous to forgive us the sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness. If we say that we haven’t sinned, we make him a liar, and his word is not in us.

refs.label: 1 John 2:1–2
refs.t: My little children, I write these things to you so that you may not sin. If anyone sins, we have a Counselor with the Father, Jesus Christ, the righteous. And he is the atoning sacrifice for our sins, and not for ours only, but also for the whole world.

refs.label: 1 John 3:6–9
refs.t: Whoever remains in him doesn’t sin. Whoever sins hasn’t seen him and doesn’t know him. Little children, let no one lead you astray. He who does righteousness is righteous, even as he is righteous. He who sins is of the devil, for the devil has been sinning from the beginning. To this end the Son of God was revealed: that he might destroy the works of the devil. Whoever is born of God doesn’t commit sin, because his seed remains in him, and he can’t sin, because he is born of God.

refs.label: Galatians 5:16–17
refs.t: But I say, walk by the Spirit, and you won’t fulfill the lust of the flesh. For the flesh lusts against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh; and these are contrary to one another, that you may not do the things that you desire.

questions.summary: Christians still sin, but they cannot be at peace with sin.
body: John says if we say we have no sin we deceive ourselves, and also that whoever is born of God does not keep on sinning. Paul asks, "Shall we sin so grace may abound? By no means!" The Christian life involves real struggle between flesh and Spirit, real confession and real growth.

questions.title: Can I know I’m saved?

refs.label: 1 John 5:11–13
refs.t: The testimony is this, that God gave to us eternal life, and this life is in his Son. He who has the Son has the life. He who doesn’t have God’s Son doesn’t have the life. These things I have written to you who believe in the name of the Son of God, that you may know that you have eternal life, and that you may continue to believe in the name of the Son of God.

refs.label: John 10:27–30
refs.t: My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me. I give eternal life to them. They will never perish, and no one will snatch them out of my hand. My Father who has given them to me is greater than all. No one is able to snatch them out of my Father’s hand. I and the Father are one.”

refs.label: Romans 8:1
refs.t: There is therefore now no condemnation to those who are in Christ Jesus, who don’t walk according to the flesh, but according to the Spirit.

refs.label: Romans 8:38–39
refs.t: For I am persuaded that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor things present, nor things to come, nor powers, nor height, nor depth, nor any other created thing will be able to separate us from God’s love which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.

refs.label: Ephesians 2:8–9
refs.t: for by grace you have been saved through faith, and that not of yourselves; it is the gift of God, not of works, that no one would boast.

questions.summary: John wrote so that believers may know they have eternal life.
questions.views: Christians differ on whether a true believer can lose salvation (Reformed "perseverance of the saints" versus Arminian views). All affirm salvation is by grace through faith.
body: Assurance rests on Christ’s finished work, not your performance. There is no condemnation for those in Christ. Fruit in your life, love for God and others, and the Spirit’s witness confirm genuine faith.

questions.title: What does the Bible say about divorce?

refs.label: Matthew 19:3–9
refs.t: Pharisees came to him, testing him, and saying, “Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife for any reason?” He answered, “Haven’t you read that he who made them from the beginning made them male and female, and said, ‘For this cause a man shall leave his father and mother, and shall be joined to his wife; and the two shall become one flesh?’ So that they are no more two, but one flesh. What therefore God has joined together, don’t let man tear apart.” They asked him, “Why then did Moses command us to give her a certificate of divorce, and divorce her?” He said to them, “Moses, because of the hardness of your hearts, allowed you to divorce your wives, but from the beginning it has not been so. I tell you that whoever divorces his wife, except for sexual immorality, and marries another, commits adultery; and he who marries her when she is divorced commits adultery.”

refs.label: Malachi 2:13–16
refs.t: This again you do: you cover Yahweh’s altar with tears, with weeping, and with sighing, because he doesn’t regard the offering any more, neither receives it with good will at your hand.
